Our Core Values:
Love
Love and care of yourself, for others and for our things.
Trust
In yourself and be honest with others, true to your word.
Respect
For yourself – doing your best and having time for other people.
Curiosity
Be open to possibilities and not make assumptions about others. Where could your life and dreams take you?
BurstowPrimary School
Our aim is to be a school of excellence and happiness at the heart of the community, where every child feels valued, successful and inspired. Burstow Primary School is an inclusive, positive environment where children are empowered to thrive. Guided by our core values of love, trust, curiosity and respect, we inspire every child to embrace their potential, build meaningful relationships, contribute positively to our community and embrace lifelong learning. We aim for every child to Be Amazing at Burstow and prepare them for success beyond our school.

pageCache.text:
Breakfast and After School Clubs
Breakfast Club
Breakfast club is run by Camp Glide
To book your sessions on their booking system: Camp glide
They provide daily healthy breakfast choices including cereal, toast, yoghurt, fruit and spreads with usually a hot option on offer.
There are free play or structured activities before going to class.
If you have any questions: Info@campglide.co.uk or call them on 0330 113 5600
After School Club
The After School Club runs from 3- 6pm every school day apart from the end of term when the school closes at 1.30pm.
A wide range of activities are offered to the children; both quiet relaxed sessions and more active games outside.
It is possible to attend the After School Club once the family has registered and depending on session availability. There is a family registration fee of £5 and sessions cost £12 per day, which includes tea.
Registration forms and information on how to book are available from the school office. Paperwork must be completed and payment made before the children can attend.
Bookings and payment must be made 24hrs in advance, you will not be able to book a session on the day.
The club must be notified in advance if your child will not be attending a booked session, as refunds/credits cannot be given for late or non-cancellations.

PE and Sports Premium
The Government provides additional funding to improve the provision of physical education (PE) and sport in primary schools. We are committed to using this resource to develop high quality PE lessons, alongside greater opportunities for sporting competitions and clubs for all our pupils.
Our main targets in school are:
To increase the engagement of all pupils in regular physical activity
To increase the confidence, knowledge and skills of all staff in teaching PE and sport
To offer a broader experience of a range of sports and activities
To increase the school's participation in competitive sport

pageCache.pageTitle: Burstow Primary School - Educational Visits and Residentials
pageCache.text:
Educational Visits and Residentials
At Burstow, we believe that true learning happens when children are immersed in real-life experiences that spark their curiosity. By providing contexts that engage and motivate learners, we encourage them to question, investigate, and hypothesise, deepening their understanding of the world around them. Our trips and visits, which take place each half term, are closely linked to the class topics, offering children opportunities to explore in meaningful ways. These experiences may include trips to museums, historical sites, farms, or enriching activities within school, such as theatre performances, visiting speakers, or animal encounters.
As part of our commitment to pupils' Spiritual, Moral, Social & Cultural development, we also offer exciting residential trips for Year 3 and Year 6. These trips are designed to help children build team-building skills, develop resilience, and boost their confidence through problem-solving and risk-taking. Year 3 students visit High Ashurst Outdoor Learning Centre near Box Hill for a two-day adventure, while Year 6 pupils head to Norfolk Lakes for a five-day experience.
At Burstow, we’re dedicated to helping children explore the world with curiosity and confidence, discovering new ideas and building lasting memories along the way.

Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Burstow Primary School!
Our values are at the heart of everything we do. We believe in nurturing Curiosity, and fostering a love for learning. Respect is central, ensuring everyone feels valued and supported. Love binds our community, inspiring growth and kindness. Trust forms the foundation of our relationships, promoting openness, honesty, and reliability. Our vision is to be a school of excellence and happiness at the heart of the community which embodies our commitment to empowering every child to reach their fullest potential.
A warm welcome awaits you at Burstow Primary School and there's no better way to experience the spirit of our school than to visit us in person. We'd be delighted to show you around and give you a flavour of everyday life in school, introduce you to our wonderful staff and pupils, and answer any questions you might have.
We hope you will come and visit us very soon

Our Safeguarding Culture
Operation Encompass
We are part of Operation Encompass, which ensures that we receive notifications from police of any domestic abuse incidents involving children (incidents in which a child was present, ordinarily resides as the incident location or with an involved party).
Bullying is unacceptable and will not be tolerated at Burstow Primary School.
Pupils are taught how to identify bullying and how to respond to it.
We have clear procedures that are continuously reviewed to ensure they are effective and a behaviour policy which all members of staff diligently adhere to.

Our Curriculum
Individual Subject Intent
Our Curriculum at Burstow Primary School –
At Burstow, we provide a rich and ambitious maths curriculum that supports all children in mastering key concepts. Using a mastery approach, we focus on fluency, reasoning, and problem-solving through concrete, pictorial, and abstract methods. Building strong number sense and place value helps children develop the confidence to explain their thinking and solve problems effectively.
We believe maths is for everyone, and learning is inclusive and collaborative, with targeted support when needed. By promoting curiosity and resilience, children are encouraged to explore, question, and persevere. Our curriculum connects maths to real-life applications, and by deepening their understanding, we ensure that children leave Burstow confident and well-prepared for future challenges.
At Burstow, we believe that reading is fundamental to pupils’ success and underpins learning across the curriculum. We place reading at the heart of school life and aim for all pupils to become fluent, confident and enthusiastic readers. Our vision is for every child to develop the skills, knowledge and enjoyment of reading that will enable them to access the wider curriculum and foster a lifelong love of books.
To achieve this, we deliver the Read Write Inc. (RWI) phonics programme to ensure a consistent, systematic and structured approach to the teaching of early reading and writing. Pupils are taught to recognise sounds, blend to read words and segment to spell with increasing accuracy and confidence. Regular assessment ensures pupils are taught in groups matched to their phonics knowledge so that teaching is closely targeted and all children can make strong progress from their starting points. Carefully matched reading books allow pupils to apply their phonics knowledge, supporting the development of fluency and confidence as readers.
The Read Write Inc. (RWI) programme provides a consistent and systematic approach to the teaching of early reading and letter formation. Daily 45-minute, phonics lessons follow the structured RWI format and are delivered by trained staff to ensure fidelity to the programme. Pupils are assessed by the trained phonics champion regularly (6-8 weeks) and grouped according to their phonics knowledge so that teaching is closely matched to their stage of learning. Carefully matched reading books allow pupils to practise and apply their phonics knowledge, supporting the development of fluency, accuracy and confidence. Pupils take home RWI Book Bag Books to reinforce the sounds and words they are learning in school. Pupils in the Orange to Grey groups also take home the class storybook they have been reading in lessons, enabling them to re-read familiar texts at home to build confidence, fluency and expression. Consistent routines, high expectations and ongoing assessment ensure pupils make strong progress through the programme.
Early reading is a strength at Burstow. In 2025, 72% of children achieved a Good Level of Development, above the national figure of 68.3%, and 85% of pupils met the expected standard in the Year 1 Phonics Screening Check, exceeding the national figure of 80%. This strong performance reflects the consistent and robust implementation of the Read Write Inc. programme across the school. Robust assessment systems, led by the Phonics Champion, ensure that pupils are grouped accurately and that movement between groups is responsive and timely.
We use the Read Write Inc. phonics programme with daily sessions from Reception to Year 2, helping children develop a love of reading and become confident, lifelong readers. We believe reading is essential to unlocking learning across the curriculum and building a strong foundation for success.
Our classrooms are rich in language, with books and storytelling at the heart of learning. Children explore a diverse range of fiction, non-fiction, poetry, and plays, building their vocabulary and comprehension. Through oracy and daily reading activities, we empower children to develop fluency, confidence, and a deep love for literature.
Writing at Burstow Primary School
At Burstow Primary, we believe that great writers are nurtured through a structured, exciting curriculum that sparks curiosity and inspires creativity. From Reception to Year 6, children build their writing skills step by step, developing their ability to express themselves clearly and imaginatively. Our approach ensures that every child, regardless of background or need, can succeed and achieve their full potential.
We place a strong emphasis on the writing process, encouraging pupils to engage in purposeful writing through planning, drafting, editing, and publishing. By breaking writing into clear stages, we help children refine their ideas, improve their skills, and develop a greater sense of ownership over their work. This process not only builds their writing abilities but also encourages critical thinking, attention to detail, and a commitment to producing high-quality work.
Through the joy of storytelling, rich language experiences, and engaging writing tasks, children grow into articulate communicators, both in written and spoken word. By encouraging curiosity and exploration, we help children discover their own voice and develop a deep appreciation for language and literature. By the time they leave our school, they will be confident, enthusiastic writers who feel empowered to share their ideas with respect and excitement. They will be ready to take on the next steps in their learning journey with trust in their abilities and a love for the craft of writing.
Design and Technology (DT)
At Burstow Primary School we offer an engaging and high-quality Design and Technology curriculum that sparks curiosity, fuels creativity, and broadens children's imaginations. Through practical, real-life projects, children generate ideas, research, and design products that solve real-world problems, developing critical thinking and problem-solving skills and becoming responsible and reflective learners. They explore solutions that meet a range of needs and values, while learning to work both independently and collaboratively. Children progressively build on their technical knowledge and expand their technological understanding, seeing themselves as both designers and makers. They are taught to select tools and materials safely and effectively and reflect on their design choices, with opportunities to develop resilience, creativity, and decision-making skills. By the time they leave Burstow, every child will have experienced design thinking and its applications in a variety of contexts, preparing them for future challenges as confident problem solvers.
French In Key Stage 2, we bring French to life through conversations, games, and role-play. Children practice speaking and listening, building their confidence in using another language. French lessons also explore cultural aspects, helping children appreciate the wider world while learning practical language skills.
In our history curriculum, we encourage children to describe key events and significant figures, while building a chronological understanding of British, local, and world history. Pupils learn to interpret historical sources, compare similarities and differences, and draw conclusions about how the past has influenced the present. By fostering critical thinking, we encourage children to ask questions, evaluate evidence, and form their own opinions, helping them develop empathy and a deeper appreciation for the diversity of human experience.
We place a strong emphasis on exploring history from different perspectives, ensuring children gain a broad cultural awareness. Through the study of various sources and historical viewpoints, pupils gain a richer understanding of how different cultures and events have shaped the world we live in today, all while enhancing their historical vocabulary and knowledge in a structured, chronological sequence.
In Geography, we endeavour to broaden children’s real-life experiences, providing a comprehensive curriculum for all our learners. Through map work, fieldwork, and an exploration of both physical and human features, pupils will develop a global understanding, as well as the skills needed to name and locate places. Students will pose questions and seek answers as they explore their immediate locality, before journeying into the wider world beyond. Pupils will compare geographical similarities and differences, linking their learning to real-world contexts and developing critical thinking about global issues. By encouraging a sense of global awareness and responsibility, we aim to empower them to become respectful and responsible citizens, capable of navigating a complex and ever-changing world.
The study of geography is about more than just memorising places on a map. It’s about understanding the complexity of our world and appreciating the diversity of cultures that exist across continents. And in the end, it’s about using all that knowledge to help bridge divides and bring people together – Barak Obama
Music In music, children have the opportunity to practise and perform across a wide range of musical activities. Our curriculum encourages creativity through composing and understanding musical terms, helping children develop their confidence as they listen, review, and evaluate music from various cultures and periods. Through collaboration and performance, pupils will become well-rounded musicians with a deep appreciation for the role of music in society.
At Burstow, we provide an engaging and inclusive PE curriculum that encourages every child to develop a lifelong love of physical activity and sport. Through a wide range of activities, we help children develop physical activity skills for sustained periods, promoting teamwork, competitive sports, and resilience. By fostering confidence in their physical abilities, we aim to develop the fundamental skills that enable pupils to excel in a variety of sports and physical activities, while promoting a sense of achievement and enjoyment.
Our approach ensures children understand the importance of healthy, active lifestyles and physical well-being, while also learning the values of respect, fair play, and teamwork. Whether working individually or collaboratively, children are encouraged to set personal goals, reflect on their progress, and develop resilience, preparing them for future physical challenges both inside and outside of school. By the time they leave Burstow, every child will have the physical and social skills needed to thrive in sports and lead an active, healthy life, grounded in the values of respect, curiosity, trust, and love.
PSHE (Personal, Social, Health, and Economic Education)
In PSHE, we help children understand their feelings, build healthy relationships, and develop a sense of responsibility. Through discussions and group activities, children learn to communicate openly, respect others, and take care of their own well-being. We aim to prepare them for the challenges of life inside and outside of school.
Religious Education (RE) at Burstow Primary School
In RE, children explore their own beliefs and those of others, while developing a sense of respect and empathy. Through critical thinking and discussions, pupils learn to identify similarities and differences between different religions and world views, deepening their understanding of diversity. Our curriculum encourages children to engage thoughtfully with moral and ethical issues related to community, values and respect, building the foundation for informed participation in the world. Through the study of significant religious terms and vocabulary, children gain a strong understanding of the diversity of beliefs and practices around the world.
Science at Burstow Primary School
At Burstow, we aim to ignite curiosity and excitement about the world through a hands-on, enquiry-based science curriculum. Children are encouraged to explore and question the world around them, developing a deeper understanding of their environment. We promote open-mindedness and inspire pupils to ask questions, seek answers, and become independent, confident learners.
STEM is a vital part of our learning, interwoven across the curriculum and celebrated with dedicated events throughout the year. We teach children to respect the diverse narratives and contributions from different cultures that underpin many modern-day inventions, helping them appreciate the richness of global innovation. By connecting children with real-world science through workshops and community engagement, we develop a love for learning that extends beyond the classroom. At Burstow, every child is empowered to explore science in an inclusive, stimulating environment that builds the skills and knowledge they need for future success.

pageCache.pageTitle: Burstow Primary School - Our Curriculum Intent
pageCache.text:
Our Curriculum Intent
Burstow Primary School A school of excellence and happiness at the heart of the community, where every child feels valued, successful and inspired.
Our Purpose Burstow Primary School is an inclusive, positive environment where children are empowered to thrive. Guided by our core values of love, trust, curiosity and respect, we inspire every child to embrace their potential, build meaningful relationships, contribute positively to our community and embrace lifelong learning. We aim for every child to Be Amazing at Burstow and prepare them for success beyond our school.
Deliver an irresistible, broad, and balanced curriculum that is underpinned by curiosity, excels in reading, writing, and mathematics and broadens children’s knowledge across diverse subjects, linking learning to the world and their experiences.
Develop personal growth through respect, love, curiosity, and trust, shaping confident, compassionate individuals who love learning and contribute positively to their community.
Cultivate an inclusive, equitable learning environment that celebrates diversity and embeds the British Values of respect, tolerance, and fairness.
Promote storytelling, oracy and literature to create an accessible curriculum, ensuring children become confident, highly literate communicators with lasting knowledge.
Maximise every child's potential with evidence-based practices that make learning engaging, challenging and impactful.
Empower independent learners through hands-on, inquiry-based experiences that develop problem-solving skills.
Strengthen home-school partnerships, recognising the vital role of collaboration in each child's development and success.
